arxiv-2305-09105.title: Optimizing pre-scheduled, intermittently-observed MDPs
arxiv-2305-09105.creator: Patrick Zhong, Federico Rossi, Dylan A. Shell
arxiv-2305-09105.description: Abstract A challenging category of robotics problems arises when sensing incurs substantial costs. This paper examines settings in which a robot wishes to limit its observations of state, for instance, motivated by specific considerations of energy management, stealth, or implicit coordination.

arxiv-2306-12919.title: An Interactive Interface for Novel Class Discovery in Tabular Data
arxiv-2306-12919.creator: Colin Troisemaine, Joachim Flocon-Cholet, Stéphane Gosselin, Alexandre Reiffers-Masson, Sandrine Vaton, Vincent Lemaire
arxiv-2306-12919.description: Abstract Novel Class Discovery (NCD) is the problem of trying to discover novel classes in an unlabeled set, given a labeled set of different but related classes. The majority of NCD methods proposed so far only deal with image data, despite tabular data being among the most widely used type of data in practical applications.

arxiv-2308-10537.title: KGrEaT: A Framework to Evaluate Knowledge Graphs via Downstream Tasks Conference: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 21–25, 2023; Birmingham, United Kingdom Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and Know
arxiv-2308-10537.creator: Nicolas Heist, Sven Hertling, Heiko Paulheim
arxiv-2308-10537.description: Abstract . In recent years, countless research papers have addressed the topics of knowledge graph creation, extension, or completion in order to create knowledge graphs that are larger, more correct, or more diverse. This research is typically motivated by the argumentation that using such enhanced knowledge graphs to solve downstream tasks will improve performance. Nonetheless, this is hardly ever evaluated.

arxiv-2308-14692.title: Fixed loci of symplectic automorphisms of K ​ 3 [ n ] K3^{[n]} type and n n -Kummer type manifolds
arxiv-2308-14692.creator: Ljudmila Kamenova, Giovanni Mongardi, Alexei Oblomkov
arxiv-2308-14692.description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to give an explicit description of the fixed loci of symplectic automorphisms for certain hyperkähler manifolds, namely for Hilbert schemes on K3 surfaces and for generalized Kummer varieties. Here we extend our previous results from the case of involutions to more general groups.

arxiv-2407-17468.title: WildHallucinations : Evaluating Long-form Factuality in LLMs with Real-World Entity Queries
arxiv-2407-17468.creator: Wenting Zhao, Tanya Goyal, Yu Ying Chiu, Liwei Jiang, Benjamin Newman, Abhilasha Ravichander, Khyathi Chandu, Ronan Le Bras, Claire Cardie, Yuntian Deng, Yejin Choi
arxiv-2407-17468.description: Abstract While hallucinations of large language models (LLMs) prevail as a major challenge, existing evaluation benchmarks on factuality do not cover the diverse domains of knowledge that the real-world users of LLMs seek information about. To bridge this gap, we introduce WildHallucinations , a benchmark that evaluates factuality.

arxiv-2411-10895.title: Evolution of IVR building techniques: from code writing to AI-powered automation
arxiv-2411-10895.creator: Khushbu Mehboob Shaikh, Georgios Giannakopoulos
arxiv-2411-10895.description: Abstract Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems have undergone significant transformation in recent years, moving from traditional code-based development to more user-friendly approaches leveraging widgets and, most recently, harnessing the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for automated IVR flow creation. This paper explores the evolution of IVR building techniques, highlighting the industry’s revolution and shaping the future of IVR systems.

pmc-10574382.title: Constructing FeS and ZnS Heterojunction on N,S-Codoped Carbon as Robust Electrocatalyst toward Oxygen Reduction Reaction
pmc-10574382.creator: Fenglai Pei, Min Li, Yifan Huang, Qiuyun Guo, Kunming Song, Fantao Kong, Xiangzhi Cui, Stefano Agnoli
pmc-10574382.description: Highly active and cost-efficient electrocatalysts for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) are significant for developing renewable energy conversion devices. Herein, a nanocomposite Fe/ZnS-SNC electrocatalyst with an FeS and ZnS heterojunction on N,S-codoped carbon has been fabricated via a facile one-step sulfonating of the pre-designed Zn- and Fe-organic frameworks.

pmc-11322607.title: CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies trigger a paracrine regulated wave of T-cell recruitment for effective tumor killing
pmc-11322607.creator: Chen-Yi Liao, Patrick Engelberts, Andreea Ioan-Facsinay, Janna Eleonora Klip, Thomas Schmidt, Rob Ruijtenbeek, Erik H. J. Danen
pmc-11322607.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The mechanism of action of bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) directing T-cell immunity to solid tumors is incompletely understood. Here, we screened a series of CD3xHER2 bsAbs using extracellular matrix (ECM) embedded breast cancer tumoroid arrays exposed to healthy donor-derived T-cells. An initial phase of random T-cell movement throughout the ECM (day 1–2), was followed by a bsAb-dependent phase of active T-cell recruitment to tumoroids (day 2–4), and tumoroid killing (day 4–6).

pmc-11384445.title: The implementation of the guideline for the management of pediatric off-label use of drugs in China: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11384445.creator: Min Meng, Jiale Hu, Wenjuan Lei, Min Tian, Xiao Liu, Yali Lu, Enmei Liu, Shu Zhang, Zhu Han, Qiu Li, Yaolong Chen
pmc-11384445.description: BackgroundPreviously, we developed the Guidelines for the Management of Pediatric Off-Label Use of Drugs in China in addressing the need for standardization of pediatric off-label drug use. As the implementation of recommendations in Guidelines among healthcare professionals is weak, it is important to identify barriers to guideline implementation for developing appropriate strategies for specific settings and target groups.

pmc-11546117.title: Development and Characterization of a Human Mammary Epithelial Cell Culture Model for the Blood–Milk Barrier—A Contribution from the ConcePTION Project
pmc-11546117.creator: Debora La Mantia, Nina Nauwelaerts, Chiara Bernardini, Augusta Zannoni, Roberta Salaroli, Qi Lin, Isabelle Huys, Pieter Annaert, Monica Forni, Giovanni Tossetta
pmc-11546117.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). It is currently impossible to perform an evidence-based risk assessment for medication use during breastfeeding. The ConcePTION project aims to provide information about the use of medicines during lactation. The study aimed to develop and characterize an in vitro model of the blood–milk barrier to determine the extent of the milk transfer of xenobiotics, relying on either on human mammary epithelial cells (hMECs) or immortalized cell lines derived from breast tissue.

pmc-12604830.title: Isolated Small Fiber Neuropathy and Chemotherapy-Associated Cognitive Dysfunction Following Treatment for Gastric Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report of a Unique Entity
pmc-12604830.creator: Haneen A Salama, Muhammad Umair, Isabella R Rojas, Peter G Bernad
pmc-12604830.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is a poorly documented complication in oncology patients and is often overlooked due to a lack of awareness and testing. Concurrent chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment (“chemobrain”) adds diagnostic complexity. We present a rare case of a 44-year-old male who developed SFN with intact large fibers, along with progressive cognitive slowing after completing neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy for gastric adenocarcinoma. Despite normal nerve conduction and brain MRI, the patient’s autonomic testing displayed severely abnormal sudomotor and microcirculatory responses.

pmc-12877272.title: Letter to the Editor regarding “Comfort Feeding in Hospitalised People with Dementia: A Retrospective Study of Survival Following Comfort Feeding Recommendations”
pmc-12877272.creator: Rui He, Lingjia Xu
pmc-12877272.description: on survival rates, readmission rates, and the association between dysphagia severity and recommended feeding consistency. A retrospective analysis of 163 hospitalized dementia patients who received comfort feeding recommendations revealed that 42% of the patients died during their hospital stay, with a median survival of just 13 days. The 30-day and 90-day survival rates were 25% and 15%, respectively.

pmc-13096445.title: Evaluating the detection capabilities of nanopore sequencing for Borrelia burgdorferi detection in blacklegged ticks
pmc-13096445.creator: Jacob Cassens, Evan J Kipp, Lexi E Frank, Peter A Larsen, Jonathan D Oliver
pmc-13096445.description: Ticks pose substantial threats to public health. Blacklegged ticks (Ixodes scapularis) are responsible for most tick-borne diseases in the US, transmitting seven human pathogens, including the etiological agent of Lyme disease, Borrelia burgdorferi. Molecular surveillance for tick-borne pathogens has been outpaced by their emergence, revealing a critical need to develop agnostic strategies that characterize expanding and reemerging pathogens.

pmc-13175597.title: Explainable Knowledge-Guided Algorithm for Contrast Extravasation Detection on Computed Tomography
pmc-13175597.creator: Tuan D Pham, Maki Kitamura, Taichiro Tsunoyama
pmc-13175597.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective: To develop an explainable, knowledge-guided framework for automated detection of contrast media extravasation from sequential computed tomography (CT) images and to evaluate its potential to accelerate time-critical trauma triage while maintaining clinically acceptable sensitivity.Methods: A mathematical framework was formulated to explicitly encode three expert-derived diagnostic rules: 1) progressive increase of contrast outside anatomically plausible vessels, 2) appearance of contrast in non-vascular regions, and 3) localized irregularity of vessel caliber.

pmc-13608585.title: Cross-Scale Synergistic Reinforcement of Ultra-High-Performance Concrete by Cellulose Nanofibers and Polyoxymethylene Fibers: Mechanical Behavior and Microstructural Mechanisms
pmc-13608585.creator: Peng Yu, Xueyan Han, Panfei Zheng, Xinghua Liu
pmc-13608585.description: This study proposes a cross-scale reinforcement strategy for ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) using polyoxymethylene fibers (POMFs) and cellulose nanofibers (CNFs). The mechanical behavior and cross-scale synergistic reinforcement mechanisms of POMF/CNF-reinforced UHPC are systematically investigated through compressive, three-point bending, and split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) tests, together with thermogravimetric (TG) analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and pore structure characterization.
